newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway central banker wants public sector restraint.
newsitem.headline: Norway central banker wants public sector restraint.

text.p: Norway's central bank governor Kjell Storvik said on Friday urged parliament not to dilute the government's 1997 austerity budget proposal.
Storvik said in a statement that he shared the government's view that there was a clear risk of further pressure on the economy and higher cost growth next year.
"The austeriy measures now suggested are necessary," he said in a statement.
"The risk of increasing cost pressure and an unstable economic development calls for a tight fiscal policy, at least along the lines now proposed by the government."
"It is therefore important to avoid a weakening (of the budget) in the ensuing discussions," Storvik said.

Norway is ruled by a Labour minority government under pressure from the opposition right and left of centre to increase expenditure, especially in health care before the budget is finally adopted in December.
"Moderation must be shown in the public sector if we are to avoid too strong a pressure on the economy and increasing price and cost growth," Storvik said.

The central bank chief last week called for a restrictive fiscal policy and wage moderation in 1997 to keep the country's strong economy under control following higher than expected wage increases last spring.
